name: UK NCSC 2025 assessment of DPRK IT-worker targeting

attribution.legal_posture: Official national threat or intelligence assessment; criminal charge, sanctions designation, conviction, and named incident status require separate case records.

caveats: National cyber-threat assessment; criminal or sanctions outcome requires a separate legal or administrative source.
The assessment covers a reported pattern; victim, worker, facilitator, employer, account, and confirmed placement details remain unreported.
The UK official assessment describes a single assessment context; campaign boundaries remain as reported.

statements: The NCSC Annual Review 2025 assesses that UK firms are almost certainly being targeted by DPRK IT workers disguised as freelance third-country IT staff to generate regime revenue. This is country-level threat context, not evidence of a named employer, confirmed placement, compromise, prosecution, or sanctions outcome.
limitations: Preserve the NCSC's ‘almost certainly’ confidence language.
Do not infer firm names, targeting scale, successful placements, compromise, or legal outcomes.
Treat the 2025 annual review as a current official restatement, not a separate campaign or incident.
